title: Why Is Jesus Called King of Kings?
paragraphs:
Why Is Jesus Called King of Kings?
The Title That Terrified Empires, Shattered Pride, and Still Changes Lives Today
There are titles that impress people.
History is filled with men and women who climbed higher than everyone around them, collected power, commanded armies, built companies, accumulated wealth, and left their names carved into monuments.
Yet every throne eventually becomes empty.
And every human ruler eventually faces the same reality:
They are not the highest authority.
That is why one title given to Jesus Christ stands above every title ever spoken.
The title sounds majestic, but most people have never stopped to ask what it truly means.
Why would Scripture call Jesus the King of Kings?
And why does this ancient title still have the power to shake hearts, expose pride, comfort the broken, and offer hope to people carrying secrets they pray nobody discovers?
The answer begins long before Bethlehem.
The Hebrew Scriptures repeatedly reveal God as the ultimate ruler over every earthly authority.
"For God is the King of all the earth."
The Hebrew word for king is מֶלֶךְ (Melekh).
One to whom all creation ultimately answers.
While human kings fought wars over temporary territories, the God of Israel ruled over heaven, earth, time, nations, history, and eternity itself.
Every kingdom existed because He allowed it.
Every ruler breathed because He gave breath.
Every empire rose because He permitted it.
Every empire fell because He decreed it.
The prophets began speaking of a coming Messiah who would not merely represent God's kingdom.
And when He finally came, He arrived in a way nobody expected.
The King of Kings entered His creation as a servant.
The Creator became part of creation.
The One enthroned above cherubim chose a manger.
The One worshiped by angels chose weakness.
The One who spoke galaxies into existence chose human flesh.
Καὶ ὁ Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο (Kai ho Logos sarx egeneto).
Because humanity's greatest problem was never politics.
The Greek word used throughout the New Testament is ἁμαρτία (hamartia).
And the consequences touched every heart.
Some people wear their scars publicly.
Some carry regrets so heavy they still wake up at night replaying moments they wish they could erase.
Maybe you know exactly what that feels like.
Maybe there are chapters of your story you hope nobody ever reads.
Moments that still make your stomach turn.
Words you wish you could take back.
Relationships you wish you could restore.
That is where Jesus enters the story.
Not for people who have everything together.
Not for those who earned His favor.
Jesus stepped into history for sinners.
This is why the Gospel is not merely good advice.
The King came looking for His lost people.
And unlike earthly kings who demand others die for them, this King died for His people.
Revelation eventually reveals His full identity.
The apostle John sees the risen Christ returning in glory.
"On His robe and on His thigh He has a name written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS."
ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ ΒΑΣΙΛΕΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΚΥΡΙΟΣ ΚΥΡΙΩΝ (Basileus Basileōn Kai Kyrios Kyriōn).
And one day every person will stand before Him.
"At the name of Jesus every knee should bow."
Because the throne belongs to Christ.
Yet this truth is not meant merely to inspire awe.
It is meant to offer hope.
Because the One sitting on the throne still bears scars.
The King of Kings is also the Lamb who was slain.
The Judge is also the Savior.
The Ruler is also the Redeemer.
The One with authority to condemn chose instead to provide a way of forgiveness.
That is why our mission is called "From Scandal to Grace."
Because Jesus specializes in rewriting stories.
The cross proves that no failure is beyond God's ability to redeem.
And perhaps that is why this message resonates so deeply.
Because everyone has a chapter they wish they could rewrite.
Everyone has moments they would erase if given the opportunity.
But Jesus does not simply erase stories.
If this message stirred something inside you, do not keep scrolling.
What part of your story are you still trying to hide?
What burden are you still carrying?
What failure have you convinced yourself is too big for God's grace?
Your testimony may be the encouragement someone else desperately needs today.
Because at the end of history, the greatest question will never be how much money we made, how many followers we gained, how much influence we accumulated, or how successful we appeared.
The greatest question will be this:
What did we do with the King?
And the breathtaking truth of the Gospel is that the King of Kings is still inviting people home.
The crown that rules the universe is worn by the One who loved you enough to die for you.
One day every king will lay down his crown.
The King who could have crushed you chose instead to save you.
